title: Compact Ledger Patterns and Microaffordance Kit for Cost Rollouts
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: Define a compact, legible ledger pattern and a small set of microaffordance components for cost-focused rollouts and dashboard rows. This ticket produces a Figma-ready component kit (ledger rows, compact metric chips, inline rollout controls, and status affordances) plus a token mapping and handoff spec for engineering. Scope: 1) compact row anatomy for high-density cost tables, 2) microaffordance primitives (small toggles, inline CTA chips, contextual kebabs), 3) token mapping (spacing, elevation, semantic color tokens for status/cost deltas), 4) responsive collapse rules (desktop -> dense mobile), 5) accessibility guidelines (focus order, hit target, contrast), 6) example rollouts and canary state variants. Out of scope: full charting components and global grid refactor.
comments: 2026-02-18 Sofia Patel: Kickoff — aligned with PM to prioritize dense cost rows in the upcoming Console release. Agreed success metric: 20% token density improvement without measurable loss in glanceability (validated by 5 internal usability sessions).

2026-02-24 Jonah Reyes: Prototype v1 uploaded. Focused on three variants: baseline (current density), condensed (8px vertical padding), and compressed (4px padding + icon-only affordances). Need engineering feasibility check for 4px hit targets.

2026-03-01 Design Review: Feedback from Eng (Arjun): compressed variant may conflict with focus outlines at 4px; recommend 6px min vertical. Accessibility (Maya): icon-only affordances must have text alternatives and 44px touch area when collapsed into touch mode.

2026-03-04 PM Review (Elias): Prefer condensed variant as default for customers on Dedicated; add an account-level toggle to enable compressed view for power users. Add analytics hooks for toggle usage.

2026-03-06 Engineering follow-up (PR stub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/8790 — implements ledger token CSS variables and a basic row component. Notes: kernel for dynamic density via CSS custom props added. Blocker: vertical rhythm conflict with existing panel gutters.

2026-03-08 Usability check with 6 product designers: condensed variant scored highest for information retrieval time; compressed variant faster for scanning but had higher error rate in pointing tasks.

2026-03-10 Sofia: Updated tokens and renamed semantic tokens to cost-critical / cost-neutral / cost-positive. Preparing final handoff docs and accessibility checklist for engineering. Moving ticket to In Review.
decisions: Default to 'condensed' density (6px vertical padding) for all customers; provide an opt-in 'compressed' toggle for advanced users.
Use semantic color tokens: token.cost-raise (red-60), token.cost-drop (green-60), token.neutral (gray-600) to keep mapping consistent across dashboards and rollouts.
Microaffordances (inline chips, small kebab menus) must maintain a minimum interactive area of 44x44px when rendered on touch screens; use visual compression only for visual density, not hit area.
Handoff format will be: Figma component library with a token map CSV and a short CSS var spec. Engineering PR must reference the Figma file and CSV in the changelist.
review_feedback: PM (Elias): Add analytics events for 'density_toggle' and 'affordance_click' before launch.
Accessibility (Maya): Ensure color token pairs meet AA contrast at condensed density when paired with small numeric chips.
Engineering (Arjun): Request a fallback layout that avoids overlaps with dynamic metrics when >3 badges are present.
Design (Lina): Suggest micro-animations for rollout transitions to reduce perceived jitter when rows collapse/expand. Keep motion subtle and optional.
